reason: This text passage describes the plagues inflicted upon Egypt (frogs, boils, hail, locusts, and darkness) as divine signs to compel Pharaoh to release the Hebrews from slavery. The passage explicitly shows that the Hebrew people themselves are NOT suffering during these events—Israel's land of Goshen is specifically protected from the plague of flies ('וְהִפְלֵיתִי בַיּוֹם הַהוּא אֶת־ אֶרֶץ גֹּשֶׁן'), and during the plague of darkness, 'all the children of Israel had light in their dwellings' (וּלְכָל־ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הָיָה אוֹר בְּמוֹשְׁבֹתָם). The leaders Moses and Aaron are portrayed as executing divine wonders against Egypt, not as blaming the Hebrew people for suffering or telling them it is their own fault.
